sources.title: ComicsBoxx: Secret Warriors omnibus issue-by-issue recap

events.issue: The Mighty Avengers (2007) #13 / Secret Invasion (2008) recruitment
events.observation: Fury selects and contacts the young superpowered recruits individually; Marvel identifies Yo-Yo as one of his Secret Warriors.
HYDRA's Gorgon severely injures Yo-Yo; Marvel confirms the injury, while the independent issue index identifies this Gorgon as Tomi Shishido.
Stonewall and Yo-Yo make a personal visit to imprisoned Carl Creel, Stonewall's father; independent character account supplies the accompaniment detail.
Stonewall confronts his imprisoned father Carl Creel; Marvel character dossier calls their exchange terse.
Gateway tutors Eden in using his spatial and temporal transport abilities; Marvel identifies Gateway as his teacher.
Marvel identifies Sebastian Druid as the son of Doctor Druid and notes his inherited mystical ability.
After Sebastian is benched, Garrett trains him physically and in using his magic; issue-level details derive from an independent recap.
Sebastian is benched as a team liability; an independent recap says Fury sent Garrett to train him.

events.issue: The Mighty Avengers (2007) #13; Secret Warriors (2009) recruitment
events.observation: Marvel says Fury personally contacts each future Secret Warrior; Alexander Aaron is among the recruits, and Fury later negotiates with Ares about him.
Marvel identifies J.T. as Quake's romantic partner; an independent issue recap reports that Daisy does not know he is working for HYDRA.
J.T. secretly works for Baron Strucker while serving Fury's team; Marvel's dossier and #16 solicitation both document betrayal.
J.T. acts as a HYDRA mole inside Fury's organization, violating his mission allegiance.
An independently summarized sequence says Fury catches the falling J.T., confronts him about the betrayal, then deliberately releases his hand.
Ares is Alexander's father; #10 addresses their relationship and Alexander's divine status before a council of gods.
Marvel's #10 synopsis explicitly describes a deal Fury struck with Ares concerning Ares' son Alexander.
In the HYDRA Gehenna battle, Tomi Shishido's Gorgon fights and kills Alexander; #22 shows the aftermath. Specific lethal sequence is independent issue-level evidence.

J.T. Slade and J.T. James refer to the same Secret Warriors Hellfire.
